zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Shuʿarāʾ
Meccan
﷽
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿طسم﴾ — it was read with the nūn assimilated (idghām) into the mīm and the letters joined to one another; and it was read "طَسِينْ مِيمْ", pronouncing the nūn distinctly and pausing on the nūn. It is also permissible — though I know of no one who read it so — to say "طَسِمِيمًا", making "طسم" a name for the sura, in the manner of his saying "خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ" (fifteen); but reciting it so is not permitted.

zajjaj:2-2.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿تِلْكَ آياتُ الكِتابِ المُبِينِ﴾ — there are two ways (wajhān) in it. One of them is on the meaning that they had been promised the Quran on the tongue of Moses, so the meaning would be: "these are the verses of the Book which you were promised on the tongue of Moses"; and (the other is) on the meaning: "these are the verses of the clear Book". We have explained that at the beginning of Sūrat "al-Baqara", in His saying: ﴿الم﴾ [al-Baqara: 1] ﴿ذَلِكَ الكِتابُ﴾ [al-Baqara: 2].

zajjaj:3-3.t: His saying: ﴿لَعَلَّكَ باخِعٌ نَفْسَكَ ألا يَكُونُوا مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ — Abū ʿUbayda said: its meaning is "destroying yourself"; and it was said: "killing yourself". This is like His saying: ﴿فَلَعَلَّكَ باخِعٌ نَفْسَكَ عَلى آثارِهِمْ إنْ لَمْ يُؤْمِنُوا بِهَذا الحَدِيثِ أسَفًا﴾ [al-Kahf: 6]. The position of "أنْ" is accusative, as a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose); the meaning is: "perhaps you are killing yourself because of their abandoning faith". So Allah, Glorified is He, informed him that had He wished to send down what would compel them to obedience, He would have been able to do so; but He, Mighty and Majestic, has laid upon them worship by which, together with faith, they merit reward, and He sent down for them signs by which the truth becomes clear to whoever seeks it. As for if punishment were sent down upon everyone who turns obstinately from the truth at the time of his obstinacy, he would submit under compulsion and believe with the faith of one who finds no way of escape from faith.

zajjaj:4-4.t:
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿فَظَلَّتْ أعْناقُهم لَها خاضِعِينَ﴾ — its meaning is "then their necks would remain (fa-taẓallu)", because in the apodosis (jazāʾ) the past-tense form occurs with a future meaning. You say "إنْ تَأْتِنِي أكْرَمْتُكَ", meaning "أُكْرِمْكَ" (I will honour you); and "إنْ أتَيْتَنِي وأحْسَنْتَ", meaning "and you do good and act well". He said "خاضِعِينَ" while mentioning the necks, because the meaning of the submission of the necks is the submission of the owners of the necks; since submission is only by the submitting of the necks, it is permissible to make the statement about the muḍāf ilayhi, as the poet said:
رَأتْ مَرَّ السِّنِينَ أخَذْنَ مِنِّي ∗∗∗ كَما أخَذَ السِّرارُ مِنَ الهِلالِ
(She saw the passing of the years — they took from me as the dark of the month takes from the crescent.)
Since years exist only by passing, he made the statement about the years, even though he had annexed the passing to them. Similar to that also is the saying of the poet:
مَشَيْنَ كَما اهْتَزَّتْ رِماحٌ تَسَفَّهَتْ ∗∗∗ أعالِيَها مَرُّ الرِّياحِ النَّواسِمِ
(They walked swaying as lances sway whose tips the passing of the gentle breezes has set tossing.)
as though he said "the winds set them tossing" (tasaffahathā, feminine), since winds exist only by passing. It came in the exegesis that by "أعْناقُهم" their great ones and their chiefs are meant; and it came in the language that "أعْناقُهم" means their groups: one says "جاءَ لِي عُنُقٌ مِنَ النّاسِ", that is: a group. Some of them mentioned another way; they said: "فَظَلَّتْ أعْناقُهم لَها خاضِعِينَ هم", with "هم" implied, and recited:
تَرى أرْباقَهم مُتَقَلِّدِيها كَما ∗∗∗ صَدِئَ الحَدِيدُ عَنِ الكُماةِ
(You see their halters — wearing them round their necks — as iron grows rusty on armoured warriors.)
This is not permissible in the Quran. It is, on the basis of the badal of error (badal al-ghalaṭ), permissible in poetry, as though he said: "he sees their halters, he sees those wearing them", as though he said: "he sees a people wearing their halters". Had it been on the omission of "هم", it would also have been among what is permissible in poetry.

zajjaj:6-6.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَسَيَأْتِيهِمْ أنْباءُ ما كانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ﴾: "أنْباءُ" means reports. The meaning is: "they will come to know the news of that at the Resurrection"; and it is possible that some of that is hastened for them in this world, such as what befell them on the Day of "Badr".

zajjaj:7-7.t: His saying: ﴿أوَلَمْ يَرَوْا إلى الأرْضِ كَمْ أنْبَتْنا فِيها مِن كُلِّ زَوْجٍ كَرِيمٍ﴾: the meaning of "زَوْجٍ" is: kind; and the meaning of "كَرِيمٍ" is: praiseworthy in what is needed, with the meaning of "of every beneficial kind", the causing of which to grow and the bringing of which into being none is able to do except the Lord of the worlds.

zajjaj:8-8.t:
Then He said: ﴿إنَّ في ذَلِكَ لآيَةً﴾: an indication that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is One, and that created things are signs pointing to the Creator being One; there is nothing like Him.
His saying: ﴿وَما كانَ أكْثَرُهم مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ means: most of them were not going to believe, that is: Allah knew that most of them would never believe, as He said: ﴿وَلا أنْتُمْ عابِدُونَ ما أعْبُدُ﴾ [al-Kāfirūn: 3], that is: you are not worshipping what I worship now; ﴿وَلا أنْتُمْ عابِدُونَ ما أعْبُدُ﴾ [al-Kāfirūn: 5], in what is to come; and like His saying in the story of Noah, peace be upon him: ﴿أنَّهُ لَنْ يُؤْمِنَ مِن قَوْمِكَ إلا مَن قَدْ آمَنَ﴾ [Hūd: 36], so He informed him that most of them would not believe.

zajjaj:10-10.t: His saying: ﴿وَإذْ نادى رَبُّكَ مُوسى أنِ ائْتِ القَوْمَ الظّالِمِينَ﴾: the position of "إذْ" is accusative, on the meaning: "and recite this story among what you recite". The proof of that is His saying, conjoined to this story: ﴿واتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَبَأ إبْراهِيمَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 69].

zajjaj:13-13.t: His saying: ﴿وَيَضِيقُ صَدْرِي ولا يَنْطَلِقُ لِسانِي﴾ — with the accusative and the nominative. Whoever reads the nominative conjoins it to "أخافَ", on the meaning: "I fear, and my breast is constricted"; and whoever reads the accusative conjoins it to "أنْ يُكَذِّبُونِ وأنْ يَضِيقَ صَدْرِي وألّا يَنْطَلِقَ لِسانِي". The nominative is more common in recitation. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿فَأرْسِلْ إلى هارُونَ﴾, that is: "so that he may help me and support me in my affair"; this was omitted because there is an indication of it in the speech.

zajjaj:14-14.t: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَلَهم عَلَيَّ ذَنْبٌ فَأخافُ أنْ يَقْتُلُونِ﴾: by the "sin" he means the man whom he struck with his fist and killed: I fear that they will kill me for my killing him.

zajjaj:15-15.t: ﴿قالَ كَلا فاذْهَبا بِآياتِنا﴾: "كَلّا" is a deterrent and a rebuke against persisting in this supposition, as though He said: desist from this supposition and trust in Allah.

zajjaj:16-16.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَقُولا إنّا رَسُولُ رَبِّ العالَمِينَ﴾ means: "we are the message of the Lord of the worlds", that is: "bearers of the message of the Lord of the worlds". The poet said:
لَقَدْ كَذَّبَ الواشُونَ ما بُحْتُ عِنْدَهم ∗∗∗ بِسِرٍّ ولا أرْسَلْتُهم بِرَسُولِ
(The slanderers have lied: I disclosed no secret to them, nor did I send them with any message.)

zajjaj:17-17.t: His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿أنْ أرْسِلْ مَعَنا بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ﴾: the position of "أنْ" is accusative; the meaning is: "we have been sent so that you send", that is: "so that you send the Children of Israel with us".

zajjaj:18-18.t: ﴿قالَ ألَمْ نُرَبِّكَ فِينا ولِيدًا﴾, that is: as a newborn, when you were born. ﴿وَلَبِثْتَ فِينا مِن عُمُرِكَ سِنِينَ﴾ — "مِن عُمْرِكَ" with the mīm quiescent is permissible, and "مِن عَمْرِكَ" with fatḥa on the ʿayn is permissible. One says "العُمْرُ", "اَلْعُمُرُ" and "اَلْعَمْرُ" for a person's lifetime; but in an oath nothing is permissible except "لَعَمْرُ اللَّهِ", nothing else, with fatḥa on the ʿayn. Sībawayh, al-Khalīl and all the Basrans mentioned that (the word in) the oath has fatḥa and nothing else. So Pharaoh reckoned it against Moses that he had raised him as a child from the time he was born until he grew up.

zajjaj:19-19.t: ﴿وَفَعَلْتَ فَعْلَتَكَ الَّتِي فَعَلْتَ﴾ — al-Shaʿbī read "فِعْلَتَكَ" with kasra on the fāʾ; the fatḥa is better and more common, because he means: "you killed the person, your (single) killing", on the pattern of the single instance. Al-Shaʿbī read it with the meaning: "and you killed in the manner of killing that you know", because he killed him with a single blow of the fist. One says "جَلَسْتُ جَلْسَةً" meaning "one time", and "جَلَسْتُ جِلْسَةً" with kasra meaning the manner of sitting. ﴿وَأنْتَ مِنَ الكافِرِينَ﴾ — there are two ways in it. One of them: "of those ungrateful for my favour"; the other: "and you are of the disbelievers by your killing the one you killed". So Moses ﷺ denied disbelief and admitted that this deed of his had been ignorance, and said: ﴿قالَ فَعَلْتُها إذًا وأنا مِنَ الضّالِّينَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 20], that is: of the ignorant. It has been read: "وَأنا مِنَ الجاهِلِينَ".

zajjaj:21-21.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَوَهَبَ لِي رَبِّي حُكْمًا﴾: the Torah is meant, in which is the judgement of Allah.

zajjaj:22-22.t:
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَتِلْكَ نِعْمَةٌ تَمُنُّها عَلَيَّ أنْ عَبَّدْتَ بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ﴾ — the exegetes took it as a denial that this could be a favour, as though he said: "so what favour do you have over me in your having enslaved the Children of Israel?!". The wording is the wording of a statement (khabar), and the meaning can be taken as they said, given that its wording is that of a statement; and in it there is a rebuke to the one addressed, as though he said to him: "this is a favour — that you took the Children of Israel as slaves!", by way of rebuking Pharaoh. The wording requires that Moses ﷺ said: "this is a favour because you took the Children of Israel as slaves and did not take me as a slave". One says "عَبَّدْتُ الرَّجُلَ" and "أعْبَدْتُهُ": I took him as a slave. The position of "أنْ" is nominative as a badal (substitute) for "نِعْمَةٌ", as though he said: "and that is a favour: your enslaving the Children of Israel and your leaving me not a slave". It is also possible for "أنْ" to be in the position of the accusative, the meaning being: "it only became a favour to me because you enslaved the Children of Israel", that is: "had you not done what you did, my family would have looked after me and would not have cast me into the river; so it only became a favour through the affliction you inflicted". The poet said, on "أعْبَدْتُ" meaning "I took as a slave":
عَلامَ يُعْبِدُنِي قَوْمِي وقَدْ كَثُرَتْ ∗∗∗ فِيهِمْ أباعِرُ ما شاؤُوا وعِبْدانُ؟
(Why do my people take me as a slave, when among them camels and slaves have multiplied, as many as they please?)

zajjaj:23-23.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿قالَ فِرْعَوْنُ وما رَبُّ العالَمِينَ﴾ — Moses ﷺ answered him with that which is an indication of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, through what He created, the like of which created beings are unable to produce. He said: ﴿رَبُّ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ وما بَيْنَهُما إنْ كُنْتُمْ مُوقِنِينَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 24]. Pharaoh was perplexed and gave no answer back by which to refute this statement, so he said to those around him: ﴿ألا تَسْتَمِعُونَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 25]. Moses increased him in clarity and said: ﴿رَبُّكم ورَبُّ آبائِكُمُ الأوَّلِينَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 26]. He did not answer him this time either, but said: ﴿إنَّ رَسُولَكُمُ الَّذِي أُرْسِلَ إلَيْكم لَمَجْنُونٌ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 27]. Then Moses said, in further clarification: ﴿قالَ رَبُّ المَشْرِقِ والمَغْرِبِ وما بَيْنَهُما إنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 28]. In none of these things did he answer him with a refutation of his argument.

zajjaj:29-29.t:
﴿قالَ لَئِنِ اتَّخَذْتَ إلَهًا غَيْرِي لأجْعَلَنَّكَ مِنَ المَسْجُونِينَ﴾ — so he increased him in clarity and argued with what he and the assembly around him witnessed: ﴿قالَ أوَلَوْ جِئْتُكَ بِشَيْءٍ مُبِينٍ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 30] ﴿قالَ فَأْتِ بِهِ إنْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الصّادِقِينَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 31] ﴿فَألْقى عَصاهُ فَإذا هي ثُعْبانٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 32]. The thuʿbān is the large kind of snake.
If someone says: how then does it come: ﴿فَإذا هي ثُعْبانٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 32], while in another place: ﴿تَهْتَزُّ كَأنَّها جانٌّ﴾ [al-Naml: 10], and the jānn is the small kind of snake? The answer: this is among what indicates the greatness of the sign; that is, its form was the form of the thuʿbān, while its quivering, its motion and its nimbleness were like the quivering and nimbleness of the jānn.

zajjaj:33-33.t: ﴿وَنَـزَعَ يَدَهُ فَإذا هي بَيْضاءُ لِلنّاظِرِينَ﴾: he drew his hand from the opening of his garment and brought it out white with a luminous whiteness, without harm (sūʾ), that is: without leprosy. He (Pharaoh) had no way of repelling what he witnessed except to say: this is sorcery: ﴿قالَ لِلْمَلإ حَوْلَهُ إنَّ هَذا لَساحِرٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 34]; so he made the miraculous sign sorcery.

zajjaj:35-35.t: Then he humbled himself and submitted to those who were among his followers, and said: ﴿يُرِيدُ أنْ يُخْرِجَكم مِن أرْضِكم بِسِحْرِهِ فَماذا تَأْمُرُونَ﴾ ﴿قالُوا أرْجِهْ وأخاهُ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 36] — with kasra on the hāʾ and with ḍamma, and with the yāʾ and the wāw: "أرْجِهِي" and "أرْجِهُو وأخاهُ". ﴿وابْعَثْ في المَدائِنِ حاشِرِينَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 36]. The meaning of "أرْجِهْ" is: postpone him; and it came in the exegesis: detain him and his brother; the meaning is one. Its interpretation is: postpone him from this present time of yours, and postpone completing the debate with him until the sorcerers are gathered for you.

zajjaj:38-38.t: His saying: ﴿فَجُمِعَ السَّحَرَةُ لِمِيقاتِ يَوْمٍ مَعْلُومٍ﴾ — this made it unnecessary to say: "so he sent and gathered the sorcerers".

zajjaj:42-42.t: His saying: ﴿قالَ نَعَمْ وإنَّكم إذًا لَمِنَ المُقَرَّبِينَ﴾, that is: you will have, along with your wage and your reward for overcoming Moses if you overcome him, in addition to that benefit, nearness and closeness with me. It is read "أئِنَّ لَنا لَأجْرًا" as a question; and "إنَّ لَنا لَأجْرًا" is permissible, not as a question but out of their confidence in him: they said "we shall surely have a reward", that is: you are one who gives us gifts and rewards us.

zajjaj:44-44.t: ﴿فَألْقَوْا حِبالَهم وعِصِيَّهم وقالُوا بِعِزَّةِ فِرْعَوْنَ إنّا لَنَحْنُ الغالِبُونَ﴾ ﴿فَألْقى مُوسى عَصاهُ فَإذا هي تَلْقَفُ ما يَأْفِكُونَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 45], that is: of what they had gathered of their stratagem and their staffs. It is related of them that they were twelve thousand sorcerers. So Moses, peace be upon him, was given victory at a time when sorcery was at its greatest and most dominant over the people of that age; and his sign was a dazzling sign in two respects: one of them, that he brought what created beings are incapable of; and the second, that the sorcerers, numbering this many, were thrown down in prostration.

zajjaj:47-47.t:
﴿قالُوا آمَنّا بِرَبِّ العالَمِينَ﴾ — so they surrendered the matter to Allah, and what cannot be repelled became clear to them. Likewise the Prophet ﷺ was sent when the Arabs were at their most poetic, their most eloquent in oratory and their most articulate; and he called them to faith in Allah with the signs which the Prophet ﷺ brought and with the Quran, by which he challenged them to produce a sura like it, and they were unable to produce a sura like it. It is also related that the sorcerers were nineteen thousand.
His saying: ﴿فَلَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 49]: the lām has entered upon "سَوْفَ" with the meaning of tawkīd (emphasis). The Kufans did not permit "إنَّ زَيْدًا لَسَوْفَ يَقُومُ", yet the entry of the lām upon سَوْفَ has occurred, and that is because the lām is emphatic.

zajjaj:49-49.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿لأُقَطِّعَنَّ أيْدِيَكم وأرْجُلَكم مِن خِلافٍ﴾ — it is related in the exegesis that the first to cut off (hands and feet) and to crucify was Pharaoh.

zajjaj:50-50.t: ﴿قالُوا لا ضَيْرَ إنّا إلى رَبِّنا مُنْقَلِبُونَ﴾, that is: there is no harm to us in what befalls us in this world, along with our hope of forgiveness.

zajjaj:51-51.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إنّا نَطْمَعُ أنْ يَغْفِرَ لَنا رَبُّنا خَطايانا أنْ كُنّا أوَّلَ المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ — with fatḥa on "أنْ", that is: because we were the first of the believers. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that they were the first believers among the people of their age; but I do not think he knew the report in the exegesis, because it came in the exegesis that those who were with Moses, peace be upon him, were six hundred thousand, and it was said: six hundred and seventy thousand. Rather, the meaning of ﴿أنْ كُنّا أوَّلَ المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ is: the first to believe in this situation, upon the appearance of Moses's sign, when they had thrown down their ropes and their staffs and had exerted themselves in their sorcery. One says "لا ضَيْرَ" and "لا ضَوْرَ" with the meaning of "لا ضُرَّ" and "لا ضَرَرَ" (no harm).

zajjaj:52-52.t: His saying: ﴿وَأوْحَيْنا إلى مُوسى أنْ أسْرِ بِعِبادِي﴾: one says "أسْرى، يُسْرِي" when one travels by night; and "سَرى يَسْرِي" — it was said that it too has the meaning of "أسْرى، يُسْرِي".

zajjaj:53-53.t:
His saying: ﴿فَأرْسَلَ فِرْعَوْنُ في المَدائِنِ حاشِرِينَ﴾, that is: he sent those who would gather the army for him; its meaning is: "so he gathered his host". Then he said: ﴿إنَّ هَؤُلاءِ لَشِرْذِمَةٌ قَلِيلُونَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 54]. "اَلشِّرْذِمَةُ" in the speech of the Arabs is: a small number. It is related that those whom he called a "شِرْذِمَة" were six hundred and seventy thousand, while Pharaoh's vanguard was seven hundred thousand, every man of them on a stallion with a helmet on his head; so he reckoned those with Moses, peace be upon him, as few in view of the great size of his own host. He said "قَلِيلُونَ", putting "قَلِيلًا" in the plural, just as one says "هَؤُلاءِ واحِدُونَ", putting واحِد in the plural, as al-Kumayt said:
فَقَدْ رَجَعُوا كَحَيٍّ واحِدِينا
(So they returned like a single tribe, as ones.)

zajjaj:55-55.t: His saying: ﴿وَإنَّهم لَنا لَغائِظُونَ﴾: one says "قَدْ غاظَنِي فُلانٌ" (so-and-so has enraged me); whoever says "أغاظَنِي" has committed a solecism (laḥn).

zajjaj:56-56.t: His saying: ﴿وَإنّا لَجَمِيعٌ حاذِرُونَ﴾ — it is also read "حَذِرُونَ". It came in the exegesis that the meaning of "حاذِرُونَ" is muʾdūn, that is: possessing equipment (adāt), that is: possessing weapons, and weapons are the equipment of war. So "اَلْحاذِرُ" is the one prepared, and "اَلْحَذِرُ" is the one alert.

zajjaj:60-60.t: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿فَأتْبَعُوهم مُشْرِقِينَ﴾, that is: at the time of sunrise. One says "أشْرَقْنا", that is: we entered upon the time of the rising of the sun. One says "شَرِقَتِ الشَّمْسُ" when it rises, and "أشْرَقَتْ" when it shines and becomes clear; and "أشْرَقْنا نَحْنُ": we entered upon sunrise.

zajjaj:61-61.t: His saying: ﴿فَلَمّا تَراءى الجَمْعانِ﴾, that is: when the host of Moses stood facing the host of Pharaoh — the companions of Moses had gone out by night — the companions of Moses said: ﴿إنّا لَمُدْرَكُونَ﴾, that is: the host of Pharaoh, this great multitude, will overtake us, and we have no strength against them.

zajjaj:62-62.t: ﴿قالَ كَلا إنَّ مَعِيَ رَبِّي سَيَهْدِينِ﴾, that is: Moses said "كَلّا", that is: desist and be restrained, for they will not overtake us.

zajjaj:63-63.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَأوْحَيْنا إلى مُوسى أنِ اضْرِبْ بِعَصاكَ البَحْرَ فانْفَلَقَ فَكانَ كُلُّ فِرْقٍ﴾, that is: every part that separated from it, ﴿كالطَّوْدِ العَظِيمِ﴾, that is: like the great mountain.

zajjaj:64-64.t: His saying: ﴿وَأزْلَفْنا ثَمَّ الآخَرِينَ﴾, that is: We brought the others near to drowning there, and they are the companions of Pharaoh. Abū ʿUbayda said: (it means) We gathered the others there; he said: and from that "مُزْدَلِفَةُ" was called "جَمْعًا" (Jamʿ). Both statements are good and fine, because gathering them is bringing them near to one another. The origin of "اَلزُّلْفى" in the speech of the Arabs is: nearness.

zajjaj:69-69.t: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿واتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَبَأ إبْراهِيمَ﴾ means: the report of Abraham.

zajjaj:71-71.t: His saying: ﴿فَنَظَلُّ لَها عاكِفِينَ﴾ means: persisting in worshipping them.

zajjaj:72-72.t: His saying: ﴿هَلْ يَسْمَعُونَكم إذْ تَدْعُونَ﴾ — if you wish, you pronounce the dhāl distinctly, and if you wish, you assimilate it into the tāʾ, making it a tāʾ, and say "إتَّدْعُونَ"; this is better in Arabic because of the closeness of the dhāl to the tāʾ. "إذَّدْعُونَ" is also permissible, but it was not read so, just as he said "مُدَّكِرْ", whose origin is "مُذْتَكِرْ".

zajjaj:77-77.t: His saying: ﴿فَإنَّهم عَدُوٌّ لِي إلا رَبَّ العالَمِينَ﴾ — the grammarians said: it is an exception not from (the kind of) the first, that is: "but the Lord of the worlds". It is also possible that they worshipped idols and other things along with Allah, so he said to them: everything you worship is an enemy to me except the Lord of the worlds, because they had made their gods equal to Allah; so he informed them that he had dissociated himself from what they worshipped except Allah, for he did not dissociate himself from worshipping Him.

zajjaj:82-82.t:
His saying: ﴿والَّذِي أطْمَعُ أنْ يَغْفِرَ لِي خَطِيئَتِي يَوْمَ الدِّينِ﴾ — it came in the exegesis that his sin was his saying: "Sarah is my sister".
And his saying: ﴿بَلْ فَعَلَهُ كَبِيرُهم هَذا فاسْألُوهُمْ﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 63], and his saying: ﴿فَقالَ إنِّي سَقِيمٌ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 89]. We have explained the meaning of his saying: ﴿بَلْ فَعَلَهُ كَبِيرُهم هَذا﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 63]. The meaning of "خَطِيئَتِي" is that the prophets are human beings, and error may befall them; except that they — the blessings of Allah be upon them — do not commit major sins, because they are protected (maʿṣūmūn), chosen over the worlds; every prophet is superior to all the people of his age.

zajjaj:84-84.t: His saying: ﴿واجْعَلْ لِي لِسانَ صِدْقٍ في الآخِرِينَ﴾ means: grant me good praise that remains until the end of time.

zajjaj:90-90.t: His saying: ﴿وَأُزْلِفَتِ الجَنَّةُ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ means: "it was brought near"; its interpretation is the nearness of their entering it and their looking at it.

zajjaj:91-91.t: His saying: ﴿وَبُرِّزَتِ الجَحِيمُ لِلْغاوِينَ﴾, that is: it was made manifest to those astray; "اَلْغاوِي" is the one astray.

zajjaj:94-94.t: His saying: ﴿فَكُبْكِبُوا فِيها﴾, that is: in Hell. The meaning of "كُبْكِبُوا" is: they were thrown on top of one another. The lexicographers said: its meaning is: they were tumbled down (duhwirū). Its reality in the language is the repetition of falling headlong, as though when he is thrown he falls on his face time after time until he settles in it — he seeks refuge with Allah from it.

zajjaj:97-97.t: His saying: ﴿تاللَّهِ إنْ كُنّا لَفي ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ﴾ ﴿إذْ نُسَوِّيكم بِرَبِّ العالَمِينَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 98] means: by Allah, we were in nothing but manifest error when we made you equal to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, so that we exalted you and worshipped you as Allah is worshipped.

zajjaj:105-105.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ المُرْسَلِينَ﴾ — the tāʾ (of the feminine) has entered although the people of Noah are masculine, because the meaning is: "the community of the people of Noah denied". He said "اَلْمُرْسَلِينَ", while it is possible that they denied Noah alone; but whoever denies one messenger of Allah's messengers has denied the whole group and opposed it, because every messenger commands belief in all the messengers. It is also possible that it is "they denied all the messengers".

zajjaj:106-106.t: His saying: ﴿إذْ قالَ لَهم أخُوهم نُوحٌ ألا تَتَّقُونَ﴾ — "أخُوهم" was said because he was from among them; and every messenger comes in the language of his people, so as to make the proof clear to them and to be clearer for them.

zajjaj:111-111.t: His saying: ﴿قالُوا أنُؤْمِنُ لَكَ واتَّبَعَكَ الأرْذَلُونَ﴾ — it is also read "وَأتْباعُكَ الأرْذَلُونَ", and in Arabic it is good and strong, because the wāw of the ḥāl (circumstantial) accompanies nouns more often in Arabic: you say "جِئْتُكَ وأصْحابُكَ الزَّيْدُونَ"; "وَصَحِبَكَ الزَّيْدُونَ" is also permissible, but more common is "جِئْتُكَ وقَدْ صَحِبَكَ الزَّيْدُونَ". It was said concerning His saying ﴿الأرْذَلُونَ﴾ that they attributed them to weaving and cupping; but crafts do no harm in matters of religion.

zajjaj:116-116.t: His saying: ﴿مِنَ المَرْجُومِينَ﴾, that is: with stones.

zajjaj:118-118.t: His saying: ﴿فافْتَحْ بَيْنِي وبَيْنَهم فَتْحًا﴾ means: "judge between me and them with a judgement"; and the judge is called "اَلْفَتّاحُ" from this.

zajjaj:119-119.t: His saying: ﴿فِي الفُلْكِ المَشْحُونِ﴾: its singular is "فَلَكٌ" and its plural is "فُلْكٌ". Sībawayh claimed that it is in the manner of "أسَدٌ" and "أُسْدٌ", and that the analogy of "فُعْلٌ" is the analogy of "فَعَلٌ". Do you not see that you say "قُفْلٌ" and "أقْفالٌ", "جُمْلٌ" and "أجْمالٌ", and likewise "أسَدٌ", "أُسْدٌ" and "آسادٌ", and "فُلْكٌ", "فَلَكٌ" and "أفْلاكٌ" in the plural? "اَلْمَشْحُونُ" is the filled; one says "شَحَنْتُهُ", that is: I filled it.

zajjaj:128-128.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿أتَبْنُونَ بِكُلِّ رِيعٍ آيَةً تَعْبَثُونَ﴾ — it is read "رِيعٍ" and "رَيْعٍ", with kasra on the rāʾ and with fatḥa. In the language it is the elevated place of the land; and from that is "كَمْ رَيْعُ أرْضِكَ؟", that is: "how high is your land?". It came in the exegesis: "بِكُلِّ رِيعٍ" means every fajj, and "اَلْفَجُّ" is the road opening through a mountain; and it also came: "on every road". His saying "آيَةً" means: a landmark.

zajjaj:129-129.t: His saying: ﴿وَتَتَّخِذُونَ مَصانِعَ لَعَلَّكم تَخْلُدُونَ﴾: the singular of "اَلْمَصانِعُ" is "مَصْنَعَةٌ" and "مَصْنَعٌ", and they are what are made for water (cisterns); and it was said: buildings. The meaning of "لَعَلَّكم تَخْلُدُونَ" is: so that you may live forever, that is: and you take buildings for living forever, not reflecting on death.

zajjaj:130-130.t: His saying: ﴿وَإذا بَطَشْتُمْ بَطَشْتُمْ جَبّارِينَ﴾ — it came in the exegesis that their assault was with the whip and the sword. He only censured them for that because it was injustice; as for (assault) in the right, assault with the whip and the sword is permissible.

zajjaj:137-137.t: His saying: ﴿إنْ هَذا إلا خُلُقُ الأوَّلِينَ﴾ — it is also read "خَلْقُ الأوَّلِينَ". Whoever read "خُلُقُ الأوَّلِينَ" with ḍamma on the khāʾ, its meaning is: the custom of the ancients; and whoever read "خَلْقُ" with fatḥa on the khāʾ, its meaning is: their fabrication and their lying. In "خَلْقُ الأوَّلِينَ" there is another way, that is: "we have been created as those before us were created; we live as they lived and die as they died, and we will not be resurrected", because they denied the resurrection.

zajjaj:148-148.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَنَخْلٍ طَلْعُها هَضِيمٌ﴾: "اَلْهَضِيمُ" is that which is pressed into itself; and it is — according to what was said — that its fresh dates are without stones. It was also said: "اَلْهَضِيمُ" is that which crumbles readily. "اَلْهَضِيمُ" in the language is the slender, pressed into itself, and there is nothing in a spathe more excellent than this.

zajjaj:149-149.t: His saying "فَرِهِينَ" — it came in the exegesis: "insolent"; and it came in the exegesis: "exultant". It was also read ﴿فارِهِينَ﴾, and the meaning of "فارِهِينَ" is: skilful. "فَرِهِينَ" is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

zajjaj:153-153.t: His saying: ﴿مِنَ المُسَحَّرِينَ﴾, that is: of those who have a saḥr, and "اَلسَّحْرُ" is the lung; that is: you are only a human being like us. It is also possible that "مِنَ المُسَحَّرِينَ" is of the pattern "اَلْمُفَعَّلِينَ" from "اَلسِّحْرُ" (sorcery), that is: of those who have been bewitched time after time.

zajjaj:166-166.t: His saying: ﴿وَتَذَرُونَ ما خَلَقَ لَكم رَبُّكم مِن أزْواجِكُمْ﴾ — Ibn Masʿūd read: "ما أصْلَحَ لَكم رَبُّكم مِن أزْواجِكم". By it the private parts are meant, and the exegesis is on that basis. That is because the people of Lot used to turn away, with women, from the private parts to the backsides; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that by this deed of theirs they were transgressors (ʿādūn), and "عادُونَ" means: wrongdoers to the utmost degree of wrongdoing. It is related that Ibn ʿUmar was asked about taḥmīḍ and said: "Do Muslims do that?!". Taḥmīḍ is the deed of the people of Lot with women and men; and whoever permits this with women is gravely mistaken.

zajjaj:168-168.t:
﴿قالَ إنِّي لِعَمَلِكم مِنَ القالِينَ﴾: "اَلْقالِي" is the one who abandons a thing, hating it with the utmost hatred.
His saying: ﴿إلا عَجُوزًا في الغابِرِينَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 171] — it came in the exegesis: "among those who remained in the punishment". "اَلْغابِرُ" in the language is the one remaining; and they recited, from al-ʿAjjāj:
فَما ونى مُحَمَّدٌ مُذْ أنْ غَفَرْ ∗∗∗ لَهُ الإلَهُ ما مَضى وما غَبَرْ
(Muhammad has not slackened since God forgave him what had passed and what remained.)
And they recited, from al-ʿAjjāj:
لا تَكْسَعِ الشَّوْلَ بِأغْبارِها ∗∗∗ إنَّكَ لا تَدْرِي مَنِ النّاتِجُ
(Do not leave the last of the milk in the udders of the dry she-camels; you do not know who will deliver their young.)
[Translator's note: this second verse is usually attributed to al-Ḥārith ibn Ḥilliza, not al-ʿAjjāj; the attribution is translated as written.]
"أغْبارُها" is what remains of the milk in the teats of the she-camel.

zajjaj:176-176.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿كَذَّبَ أصْحابُ الأيْكَةِ المُرْسَلِينَ﴾: "اَلْأيْكَةُ" is dense, intertwined trees. One says "أيْكَةٌ" and "أيْكٌ", like "أجْمَةٌ" and "أجْمٌ", the distinction between its singular and its plural being the hāʾ. It is said in the exegesis that these Companions of the Thicket were people of dense, intertwined trees; and it is said that their trees were the dawm, and the dawm is the doum palm (muql). Most of the readers keep the alif and lām in "اَلْأيْكَةِ"; Abū ʿAmr and most of the readers read it so. The people of Medina read "أصْحابُ لَيْكَةِ" with fatḥa on the lām, and when one pauses on "أصْحابُ" he says "لَيْكَةِ المُرْسَلِينَ" [Translator's note: as written; with the Medinan reading the final vowel would be fatḥa]. It is likewise without alif in the codex (muṣḥaf) in this sura, and likewise also in Sūrat "Ṣād", without alif, while in the rest of the Quran it is with alif. It is permissible — and it is very good — to say "كَذَّبَ أصْحابُ لايْكَةِ المُرْسَلِينَ", without alif in the writing, with kasra, on the basis that the origin is "اَلْأيْكَةِ" and the hamza has been dropped, so that it was said "لَيْكَةَ". The Arabs say "اَلْأحْمَرُ جاءَنِي", and when they drop the hamza they say "اَلَحْمَرُ جاءَنِي", with fatḥa on the lām and keeping the connecting alif (alif al-waṣl); and they also say "لاحْمَرُ جاءَنِي", meaning "اَلْأحْمَرُ". The retention of the alif and lām in both of them in the rest of the Quran indicates that the omission from it of the hamza, which is the connecting alif, is in the manner of their saying "لاحْمَرُ". Abū Isḥāq [Translator's note: i.e. al-Zajjāj himself] said: I mean that reading "لَيْكَةِ" in the genitive, intending "اَلْأيْكَةِ" with the lām, is better than making it "لَيْكَةِ" without supposing the alif and lām and giving it fatḥa because it is a diptote — because "لَيْكَةَ" is not known; it is only "أيْكَةٌ" for the singular and "أيْكٌ" for the plural. So the best reading in it is the kasra with the dropping of the hamza, in agreement with the codex. The people of Medina read the fatḥa according to what came in the exegesis that the name of the city belonging to those to whom Shuʿayb, peace be upon him, was sent was "لَيْكَةُ". Abū ʿUbayd al-Qāsim ibn Sallām used to prefer the reading of the people of Medina, and the fatḥa, because "لَيْكَةَ" is a diptote; and he mentioned that he preferred that because it agrees with the written text, together with what came in the exegesis — as though the city is called "اَلْأيْكَةَ" and the thicket that contains these trees is called "اَلْأيْكَةَ". The kasra is good, as we have described, and I believe it has indeed been read so.

zajjaj:184-184.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿والجِبِلَّةَ الأوَّلِينَ﴾ is conjoined to the kāf and mīm; the meaning is: "fear Him who created you and created the earlier generations (al-jibilla)". It is also read "والجُبُلَّةَ" with ḍamma on the jīm and the bāʾ; and "والجِبْلَةَ الأوَّلِينَ" and "والجُبْلَةَ الأوَّلِينَ" are permissible. As for the first two, they are read; and these two are permissible.

zajjaj:187-187.t: His saying: ﴿فَأسْقِطْ عَلَيْنا كِسَفًا مِنَ السَّماءِ﴾ — and "كِسْفًا"; both are read. Whoever read "كِسْفًا" with the sīn quiescent, its meaning is: "a portion"; and whoever read "كِسَفًا", its interpretation is: "pieces from the sky", the plural of "كِسْفَةٌ" — "كِسَفٌ", like "كِسْرَةٌ" and "كِسَرٌ".

zajjaj:189-189.t: His saying: ﴿فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَأخَذَهم عَذابُ يَوْمِ الظُّلَّةِ﴾: "اَلظُّلَّةُ" was a cloud that overshadowed them, so they gathered beneath it seeking refuge in it from the heat that had afflicted them that day; then it closed in upon them, and it was among the days of greatest punishment in this world. ﴿إنَّهُ كانَ عَذابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ﴾ — had it been outside the Quran, "عَظِيمًا" would have been permissible; but the genitive is better, as the Quran has it.

zajjaj:193-193.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿نَـزَلَ بِهِ الرُّوحُ الأمِينُ﴾ ﴿عَلى قَلْبِكَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 194] — it is also read "نَزَّلَ بِهِ الرُّوحَ الأمِينَ", the meaning being: "Allah sent down with it the Trustworthy Spirit". "اَلرُّوحُ الأمِينُ" is Gabriel, peace be upon him.
His saying: ﴿عَلى قَلْبِكَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 194] means: he descended upon you and your heart retained it and it became firm, so you will never forget it nor anything of it, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿سَنُقْرِئُكَ فَلا تَنْسى﴾ [al-Aʿlā: 6].

zajjaj:196-196.t: His saying: ﴿وَإنَّهُ لَفي زُبُرِ الأوَّلِينَ﴾ — its interpretation, and Allah knows best, is that the mention of Muhammad, peace be upon him, and the mention of the Quran are in the scriptures of the ancients. "اَلزُّبُرُ" are the books: "زَبُورٌ" and "زُبُرٌ", like your saying "رَسُولٌ" and "رُسُلٌ"; as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿يَجِدُونَهُ مَكْتُوبًا عِنْدَهم في التَّوْراةِ والإنْجِيلِ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 157].

zajjaj:197-197.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿أوَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهم آيَةً أنْ يَعْلَمَهُ عُلَماءُ بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ﴾ — when you say "يَكُنْ", the preferred choice is the accusative of "آيَةً": "أنْ يَعْلَمَهُ" is the ism of "كانَ" and "آيَةً" is the khabar of "كانَ". The meaning is: "Was not the knowledge of the scholars of the Children of Israel that the Prophet, peace be upon him, is true and that his prophethood is true a sign?!", that is: a clear token, because the scholars of the Children of Israel who believed found the mention of the Prophet, peace be upon him, written with them in the Torah and the Gospel, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said. Whoever read "أوَلَمْ تَكُنْ لَهم آيَةٌ" with the tāʾ made "آيَةً" the ism and "أنْ يَعْلَمَهُ" the khabar of "يَكُنْ". It is also permissible to say "أوَلَمْ تَكُنْ لَهم آيَةً", with the tāʾ and with "آيَةً" in the accusative, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿ثُمَّ لَمْ تَكُنْ فِتْنَتُهم إلا أنْ قالُوا﴾ [al-Anʿām: 23]. Like it is the saying of Labīd:
فَمَضى وقَدَّمَها وكانَتْ عادَةً ∗∗∗ مِنهُ إذا هي عَرَّدَتْ إقْدامُها
(He went on and drove her ahead; and urging her forward, whenever she shied away, was a habit of his.)
He put "عادَةً" in the accusative while making "كانَتْ" feminine, though it refers to the urging forward (al-iqdām), because the ism and the khabar of "كانَ" are for one thing, and the verb is adjacent to a feminine word.

zajjaj:198-198.t: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَلَوْ نَـزَّلْناهُ عَلى بَعْضِ الأعْجَمِينَ﴾: "اَلْأعْجَمِينَ" is the plural of "أعْجَمٍ", the feminine being "عَجْماءُ". "اَلْأعْجَمُ" is one who does not speak clearly, and likewise "اَلْأعْجَمِيُّ"; as for "اَلْعَجَمِيُّ", it is one who is of the race of the non-Arabs, whether he speaks clearly or not.

zajjaj:200-200.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿كَذَلِكَ سَلَكْناهُ في قُلُوبِ المُجْرِمِينَ﴾, that is: "We made their denial of it enter their hearts". Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made their requital that He sealed their hearts and made associating partners (shirk) enter them: ﴿لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ حَتّى يَرَوُا العَذابَ الألِيمَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 201]. He, Mighty and Majestic, informed that when He made shirk enter their hearts, it prevented them from faith.

zajjaj:202-202.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَيَأْتِيَهم بَغْتَةً﴾: the meaning of "بَغْتَةً" is: suddenly.

zajjaj:208-208.t: His saying: ﴿وَما أهْلَكْنا مِن قَرْيَةٍ إلا لَها مُنْذِرُونَ﴾ ﴿ذِكْرى﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 209]: "ذِكْرى" may be accusative and may be nominative, except that the case-ending does not appear on it, because its end is a shortened alif (alif maqṣūra). Whoever takes it as accusative does so as a maṣdar (verbal noun), indicated by the warning, because His saying ﴿إلا لَها مُنْذِرُونَ﴾ means: "except that it had reminders reminding (dhikrā)". It may also be in the position of the nominative, on the meaning: "our warning is a reminder", as the khabar of a mubtadaʾ. "ذِكْرًا وما كُنّا ظالِمِينَ", "with tanwīn", is also permissible, but I know of no one who read it so; so do not recite it unless a sound transmission of it is established. One says "ذَكَّرْتُهُ ذِكْرى" with the feminine alif, and "ذَكَّرْتُهُ ذِكْرًا، وتَذْكِيرًا، وتَذْكِرَةً، وذِكْرًا", and "هو مِنِّي عَلى ذُكْرٍ" (he is in my mind), nothing else.

zajjaj:210-210.t: His saying: ﴿وَما تَنَـزَّلَتْ بِهِ الشَّياطِينُ﴾ — al-Ḥasan read "اَلشَّياطُونَ", and it is an error according to the grammarians and, according to the readers, a departure from the codex. So it is not permissible as a reading, nor according to the grammarians; and even if it were permissible in grammar while the codex is against it, reciting it would not be permissible in my view.

zajjaj:212-212.t: His saying: ﴿إنَّهم عَنِ السَّمْعِ لَمَعْزُولُونَ﴾: when they were pelted with the stars, they were prevented from listening.

zajjaj:214-214.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَأنْذِرْ عَشِيرَتَكَ الأقْرَبِينَ﴾ — it is related in the exegesis that when this verse came down the Prophet ﷺ called out: "O sons of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, O sons of Hāshim, O sons of ʿAbd Manāf, O ʿAbbās — uncle of the Prophet — O Ṣafiyya — aunt of the Messenger of Allah — I cannot avail you anything against Allah; ask me of my wealth whatever you wish". It is also related that when this verse came down he climbed al-Ṣafā and called out to the nearest and then the next nearest, clan by clan.

zajjaj:215-215.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿واخْفِضْ جَناحَكَ لِمَنِ اتَّبَعَكَ مِنَ المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ — its interpretation is: "soften your wing". The Prophet ﷺ was commanded to be gentle, in addition to what Allah described him with of gentleness of character, and His exalting his character in gentleness and beautiful manners, when He said: ﴿وَإنَّكَ لَعَلى خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍ﴾ [al-Qalam: 4] ﷺ.

zajjaj:218-218.t: His saying: ﴿الَّذِي يَراكَ حِينَ تَقُومُ﴾ ﴿وَتَقَلُّبَكَ في السّاجِدِينَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 219], that is: those who pray.

zajjaj:221-221.t: His saying: ﴿هَلْ أُنَبِّئُكم عَلى مَن تَنَـزَّلُ الشَّياطِينُ﴾ — then He informed, saying: ﴿تَنَـزَّلُ عَلى كُلِّ أفّاكٍ أثِيمٍ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 222], because He, Mighty and Majestic, had said: ﴿وَإنَّهُ لَتَنْـزِيلُ رَبِّ العالَمِينَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 192], then said: ﴿نَـزَلَ بِهِ الرُّوحُ الأمِينُ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 193], and ﴿وَما تَنَـزَّلَتْ بِهِ الشَّياطِينُ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 210] is as though connected with this. Then He made known that the devils descend upon every sinful liar, that is: upon every great liar, because they used to come to Musaylima the Liar and others among the soothsayers, and cast (things) to them, and make those (soothsayers) increase in lying.

zajjaj:224-224.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿والشُّعَراءُ يَتَّبِعُهُمُ الغاوُونَ﴾ — "يَتْبَعُهم" is also permissible; with the doubling and without it. "اَلْغاوُونَ" are the devils, according to the exegesis; and it was also said: "those astray among people": when the poet satirises with what is not permissible, some people fancy that and love it, and they are those astray (al-ghāwūn); and likewise if he praises someone with what is not in him, some people love that and follow him, and they are those astray.

zajjaj:225-225.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَ أنَّهم في كُلِّ وادٍ يَهِيمُونَ﴾ — the valleys of the earth are not meant by it; it is only a parable for their speech and their poetry, as you say in ordinary speech: "I am in one valley for you and you are in another valley for me", and he does not mean that you are in a valley of the earth; he only means: "I am, for you, in a great valley of benefit, while you are, for me, in (another) kind". The meaning is that they go to extremes in blame and praise and they lie: the poet praises a man with what is not in him, and likewise with blame, so they revile. That is His saying: ﴿فِي كُلِّ وادٍ يَهِيمُونَ﴾ ﴿وَأنَّهم يَقُولُونَ ما لا يَفْعَلُونَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 226], and this is a proof that they are lying in what they say.

zajjaj:227-227.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, excepted the poets who praised the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and answered the satire of those who satirised him and satirised the Muslims, and said: ﴿إلا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ وذَكَرُوا اللَّهَ كَثِيرًا﴾, that is: poetry did not distract them from the remembrance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, nor did they make it their chief concern; they only fought in defence of the Prophet ﷺ with their hands and their tongues, and satirised those who deserved satire — and the most deserving of creation of satire is the one who denied the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and satirised him. So He said: ﴿إلا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ وذَكَرُوا اللَّهَ كَثِيرًا وانْتَصَرُوا مِن بَعْدِ ما ظُلِمُوا﴾. It came in the exegesis that those meant by "اَلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ" are ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥa al-Anṣārī, Kaʿb ibn Mālik and Ḥassān ibn Thābit al-Anṣārī.
His saying: ﴿وَسَيَعْلَمُ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا أيَّ مُنْقَلَبٍ يَنْقَلِبُونَ﴾ means that they will turn back to the Fire of Hell, abiding in it forever. "أيَّ" is accusative by His saying "يَنْقَلِبُونَ", not by His saying "وَسَيَعْلَمُ", because "أيَّ" and the other interrogatives are not governed by what precedes them.
